text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London closed higher although the market largely lagged behind the rally seen in New York. Benchmark July added $55 to close at $1,765 per tonne. September finished up $45 to close at $1,785 per tonne. Recent estimates of a sharply lower Indonesian crop did not come as a surprise to the market and were mainly the result of crop substitution and deterioration which traders were well aware of.

Following the recent collapse arabica futures in New York are tempting to consolidate and the market attracted trade support but in very nervous trade. The low open interest continues to add to volatility, traders said. It was added that industrial users seemed willing to take on some product given the magnitude of the recent sell-off. Market discussions centered on the forthcoming crop estimates by the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA). The estimate is expected to include USDA's first forecast for top-grower Brazil's 1997/98 harvest. Early estimates from industry participants in Brazil have put next season's crop at anywhere from 20 to 25 million 60-kg bags, compared with 1996/97 production of at least 27 million bags. Most US based traders said they expected the USDA figure for 1997/98 to surpass the Brazil trade forecasts, but a lack of consensus over what the number might show is likely to confine the market to a narrow range on Friday. July closed 15 points higher at 207.80 cents/lb.
MEXICO - Mexico's coffee exports in May fell 41 per cent versus last year to 270,214 bags. Mexico has little coffee and there are unlikely to be any exports until the next harvest begins in October.

BRAZIL - Brazil's coffee sales registrations as of June 6 totalled 2.32 million 60-kg bags for June, July and August, according to the June 12 bulletin of the Rio de Janeiro Coffee Center. Of this 1.32 million bags had been registered for June.
UNITED STATES - US certified coffee stocks fell by 46 bags on June 11 to 44,784 60-kg bags, down from 44,830 on June 10 but still up on the 44,002 bags registered on June 9.

GERMANY - German net green coffee imports from outside the European Union totalled 1.131 million 60-kg bags in February 1997, down from 1.26 million bags in January and 1.03 million bags in December 1996, the DKV Coffee Association said. The total in calendar year 1996 was 11.98 million bags (11.65 million in 1995). Colombia shipped 229,449 bags in February (20 percent), Brazil 201,623 bags (18 per cent), Africa 204,188 bags (18 per cent), Central and South America 328,299 bags (29 percent), Asia 167,285 bags (15 percent) and others 373 bags (0 percent).

ITALY - Italy imported 518,400 bags of coffee in January 1997, roughly the same what was imported the same month the previous year. Total imports in calendar year 1996 rose by 4 per cent to 5.608 million bags. Main suppliers of green coffee in January 1997 were Uganda (41,000 vs 35,300 bags), Zaire (40,600 vs 51,100 bags), Brazil (139,100 vs 131,400 bags) and India (45,800 vs 42,500 bags).
